subject.title: [Bug] WebChat: optimistic USER messages are lost (not just hidden) when chat.send returns before the durable transcript lands — full-replace history reconcile drops them

question: Should WebChat `chat.send` ACK only after durable user-turn persistence/progress is established, or should OpenClaw keep the current post-ACK runtime-owned persistence contract with UI-side pending-message preservation?
rationale: Both directions are plausible, but they trade off latency, duplicate suppression, session rollover, hooks, and transcript ownership; automation should not choose that contract while a conflicting gateway candidate PR is open.

options.title: Require Durable Progress Before ACK
options.body: Port the useful part of the gateway candidate onto the shared recorder/session-accessor path and prove busy same-session, rollover, media, hook, and failure cases.

options.title: Keep Runtime-Owned Persistence
options.body: Document that ACK means accepted for dispatch rather than durable transcript visibility, and close or narrow the gateway candidate accordingly.

options.title: Split UI And Gateway Work
options.body: Treat the merged UI preservation as complete and open a narrower gateway contract issue or PR for durable/progress semantics.

recommendation.title: Require Durable Progress Before ACK
recommendation.body: Port the useful part of the gateway candidate onto the shared recorder/session-accessor path and prove busy same-session, rollover, media, hook, and failure cases.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision centers on the shared user-turn recorder and transcript persistence boundary.
